text: Give me every E. coli heat-shock expression study, with their accessions.

Abstract
This study aimed to compile all relevant Escherichia coli heat‐shock expression studies retrieved from the GEO database. Using the GEO Expression Studies (GSE) collection and filtering for “heat shock” in conjunction with “Escherichia coli” and expression profiling experiments, we identified several series with detailed metadata. Based on the GEO query results, four expression studies matching our criteria were retrieved. Their accessions, along with their titles, were recorded, providing key points for further exploration of the transcriptomic responses triggered by heat shock in E. coli. The studies include datasets from high throughput sequencing platforms and one study from microarray analysis. These findings are essential for researchers interested in bacterial stress responses, specifically the transcriptional reprogramming associated with heat shock, and can serve as a foundation for further mechanistic or predictive research in microbial physiology.

I. Introduction
Background. Heat shock in bacteria such as Escherichia coli triggers specific stress responses that involve the upregulation of chaperones, proteases, and other regulatory genes. These responses help the cell to mitigate protein misfolding and maintain cellular homeostasis.  
Literature Review. The GEO query retrieved multiple expression study records (GSE series) that document heat‐shock responses in E. coli.  
Knowledge Gap. Prior to this query, the comprehensive list of heat‐shock expression studies for E. coli available in GEO had not been explicitly compiled.  
Objective & Hypothesis. The objective was to identify and list all GEO expression studies in E. coli that examine heat shock. We expected to retrieve datasets that employed either high throughput sequencing or array‐based transcriptomic profiling to study the bacterial heat‐shock response.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We filtered the GEO database for experiments annotated with “Escherichia coli”, “heat shock” and “GSE” (series) focused on expression profiling.  
Materials. The analysis used the GEO Expression Studies (GSE) dataset retrieval tool.  
Procedures. A query with the terms “Escherichia coli”, “heat shock”, and filter “GSE” was submitted. Hits were reviewed for their experiment type. Studies with expression profiling by high throughput sequencing or array (as indicated by the “experiment_type”) were selected.  
Statistical Analysis. The selection consisted of cross‐referencing experiment types to ensure only heat‐shock expression studies were included.

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1 summarizes the accessions and corresponding study titles for the retrieved heat shock expression studies.

Table 1. E. coli Heat‐Shock Expression Studies
---------------------------------------------------------------
| Accession   | Study Title                                                                  |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE330026   | The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock                 |
| GSE269907   | Cellular function of the GndA small open reading frame-encoded polypeptide during heat shock |
| GSE305476   | Deciphering Host Stress Responses for Predictable Heterologous Gene Expression in E. coli  |
| GSE289056   | Thermally adapted Escherichia coli keeps transcriptomic response during temperature upshift exposure |
---------------------------------------------------------------

Findings. Four GEO series meeting the criteria were identified from the GEO query. Each study provided a unique perspective on the E. coli heat shock response and is available via its specified accession.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The retrieved accessions represent datasets that capture heat shock-induced transcriptomic changes in Escherichia coli. They include both sequencing-based and array-based expression profiling experiments.  
Context. GSE330026 and GSE269907 focus on the role of the GndA microprotein in heat shock, while GSE305476 emphasizes stress responses during heterologous gene expression and potential heat shock activation. GSE289056 covers the adaptation following a temperature upshift.  
Limitations. The query was based on metadata matching the “heat shock” term and “expression profiling” filter; studies with heat shock components not explicitly highlighted in their metadata may be missed. Additionally, the GEO API response was truncated, but only expression studies relevant to heat shock were further considered.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. This compilation provides a clear list of expression studies for researchers interested in the heat shock response in E. coli. Future work could involve downloading and reanalyzing these datasets to compare gene expression profiles or integrate them in meta-analyses.

References
[1] GEO Series GSE330026. Available at: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE330nnn/GSE330026/  
[2] GEO Series GSE269907. Available at: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE269nnn/GSE269907/  
[3] GEO Series GSE305476. Available at: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305476/  
[4] GEO Series GSE289056. Available at: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE289nnn/GSE289056/

Acknowledgments
We acknowledge the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) and GEO for making these datasets publicly available.
